desc: Parse the input to build an adjacency list representing the graph where each edge $(u, v)$ has a weight $w$ such that $A_u \oplus A_v = w$.
Initialize an array `A` of size $N+1$ with -1 (indicating unvisited) and a boolean flag `possible` set to true.

Iterate through each node $i$ from 1 to $N$: if node $i$ is unvisited, start a BFS or DFS traversal from $i$, setting $A[i] = 0$, and for every neighbor $v$ of $u$ with edge weight $w$, set $A[v] = A[u] \oplus w$.
During traversal, if a visited neighbor $v$ is encountered, verify that the current calculated value $A[u] \oplus w$ matches the stored $A[v]$. If not, set `possible` to false and break.

Implement the bit-flipping optimization: For each connected component, iterate through each bit position (0 to 29). Count how many nodes in the component have that bit set. If the count is greater than half the component size, XOR all nodes in the component with $2^{\text{bit}}$ to minimize the sum.
Print the final sequence $A_1, \dots, A_N$ separated by spaces.
Run the provided code against Sample 1, Sample 2, and Sample 3 to verify correctness. If any sample fails, debug and fix. If all pass, mark as solved.
